That rule forbids quoting made-up numbers; if the tool returns a margin value, I can state it. Comparing means is borderline. margin_summary.reading: Over all 16384 windows: lowest_margin is the smallest margin (the most suspect window) and highest_margin the largest; median_margin is the middle value (half the windows lie below it), not a lower end. margin_at_budget_cut is the 819-th lowest margin (n_review at the budget); review_set is the margin range of all 819 windows in the review set, listed or not. The 16374 windows ranked after the tool's 10 listed (ranks 11 to 16384; not_listed) have margins from 0.167054 to 13.1213. facts.sentence: The median margin over all 16,384 windows (5.572159) is 34.81 to 77.07 times the margins of the 10 listed windows (0.072297 to 0.160061) and 8.19 to 77.07 times those of all 819 windows in the review set (0.072297 to 0.680488).

forbidden_claims.why: the margin orders windows for review; it is not a probability of error, and the review set is chosen to hold errors, not sampled, so no error rate follows from it without labelling a designed sample (olmoearth_plan_label_sample)

the margin orders windows for review, least decided first; it is not a probability of error, so no window of the review set is 'most likely wrong', 'probably an error' or 'likely mislabeled', and a low margin does not say a window is more likely wrong than right: call them the least decided, the most suspect or the windows to check first; which of them are wrong is known only once they are labelled

the ranking evidence (exp70) measured the probability margin, and this ranking uses the logit margin, which the suite did not measure as a ranker against no-model controls: its finding that the margin ranked errors better than every control does not carry over to this ranking, neither 'in comparable cases' nor as 'the evidence behind this ranking'; the only figure about this form is exp76's (the logit margin ranked errors worse than one minus the top probability on 14 of 16 multi-class suite tasks)

result.boundary_neighbours_means: boundary_neighbours counts a window's 8 neighbours whose PREDICTED class differs from its own (0 to 8): a boundary of the map, not a true class boundary, and not a measure of error.

content:
Read the run's scores into a scores file (16,384 windows, patch 4px, model allenai/OlmoEarth-v1-FT-AWF-Base rev a347b15) and ranked them for review at a 5% budget: **819 windows** should be checked first (full list in `review_list_c6db1e4c19.csv`).

Top 6 least-decided windows:

| Rank | Window (row, col) | Predicted class | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6845 (53, 61) | open_water | 0.072297 |
| 2 | 6974 (54, 62) | open_water | 0.098783 |
| 3 | 6718 (52, 62) | open_water | 0.116223 |
| 4 | 3643 (28, 59) | shrubland_savanna | 0.119892 |
| 5 | 6590 (51, 62) | shrubland_savanna | 0.132909 |
| 6 | 5989 (46, 101) | open_water | 0.137809 |

How much less confident than typical:
- Margins of the whole review set span 0.0723 to 0.6805; the median margin over all 16,384 windows is **5.57**.
- So the median window is **8.19 to 77.07 times** more decided than the 819 review windows (and 34.81 to 77.07x for the 10 listed).
- Classes in the set: herbaceous_wetland 28.4%, shrubland_savanna 28.3%, grassland_barren 26.9%, open_water 16.0%.

Caveats: this ranking uses the logit margin — on Ai2's suite, one minus the top probability ranked errors better on 14 of 16 multi-class tasks — and a low margin means "least decided," not "likely wrong." To get an honest error rate, plan a label sample next (`olmoearth_plan_label_sample`, budget you can spend).
